user.title: Tecom ChallengerPlus
user.description: Configure the Tecom ChallengerPlus integration. The integration always performs one full startup sync after connecting, so inputs, areas, relays, doors and RAS objects populate on reload. The runtime polling options below only control optional ongoing polling after startup.

connection.name: Connection
connection.description: How Home Assistant reaches the panel. These must match the comms path configured on the panel.

data_description.mode: CTPlus is the full-featured mode and the right choice for almost everyone. Printer mode is text-event only, with no control and no structured state.
data_description.host: The panel's IP address, for example 192.168.1.50.
data_description.transport: UDP is normal for a management software path. Only use TCP if the panel path is configured for it.
data_description.send_port: The port the panel listens on. Must match the Send port on the panel's comms path.
data_description.listen_port: The port Home Assistant listens on. Must match the Receive port on the panel's comms path.
data_description.bind_host: Leave as 0.0.0.0 unless Home Assistant has several network interfaces and you need to pin it to one.
data_description.tcp_role: Only used when the transport is TCP. Ignored for UDP. Default is Client (Home Assistant connects to the panel).

authentication.name: Authentication and encryption
authentication.description: Must match the panel's comms path exactly. The panel does not report a rejected credential — it simply stops responding — so a mismatch looks like the panel being offline.

data_description.auth_method: Must match the Authentication type set on the panel. Security password is the traditional method; path user name and password is supported by ChallengerPlus, Discovery, NACs and Challenger from firmware V10-06.19251.
data_description.computer_password: The 10 digit security password from the panel's comms path. The panel default is 0000000000. Note that the default cannot be used when Home Assistant connects over DHCP — set a real password on the panel in that case.
data_description.auth_username: User name for path authentication, up to 30 characters. Only used when the authentication type is path user name and password.
data_description.auth_password: Password for path authentication, up to 16 characters. Only used when the authentication type is path user name and password.
data_description.encryption_type: Must match the panel's comms path. AES is recommended. TwoFish is supported for panels already configured to use it, but is implemented in Python and is noticeably slower.
data_description.encryption_key: Must match the key on the panel exactly. Alphanumeric, up to 16 characters for the 128 bit ciphers and 32 for AES 256. The panel uses the key text directly, so a longer, mixed key is meaningfully stronger than a short numeric one.

objects.name: Panel objects
objects.description: Which inputs, areas, doors and relays exist. Listing only what you actually have keeps Home Assistant free of unused entities.

data_description.inputs_count: Creates inputs 1 to N. Use input ranges below instead if your input numbers are not contiguous.
data_description.input_ranges: Preferred over a count when inputs are not contiguous, for example 1-16,25,31. Overrides the count when set, and avoids creating entities for inputs that do not exist.
data_description.dgp_door_ranges: Doors on expanders, numbered 17 and above, for example 17-24. Recommended over the first/last door numbers below: it supports gaps and avoids creating unused door entities. Overrides first/last when set.
data_description.ras_door_ranges: Keypads and single-door controllers, numbered 1 to 16, for example 3,6. These are surfaced read-only, since a RAS may be a keypad rather than a door controller.
data_description.door_first_number: Only used when DGP door ranges above is empty. Together with the last door number this creates one contiguous block, so it cannot express gaps — prefer the ranges field.
data_description.door_last_number: Only used when DGP door ranges above is empty. Set to 0 to create no DGP doors.
data_description.relay_ranges: Preferred over a count, for example 21-23. Overrides the relay count when set, and avoids filling Home Assistant with relays that do not exist on the panel.
data_description.relays_count: Creates relays 1 to N. Use relay ranges above instead unless your relays really do start at 1 and run consecutively.

naming.name: Naming from export.panel
naming.description: Optionally apply friendly names from a CTPlus export file. Name-only: no entities are created or removed.

data_description.panel_export_path: Full path to a CTPlus export file, for example /config/export.panel. Leave empty to skip.
data_description.panel_export_rename_areas: Apply area names from the export file.
data_description.panel_export_rename_inputs: Apply input names from the export file.
data_description.panel_export_rename_doors: Apply door names from the export file.
data_description.panel_export_rename_relays: Apply relay names from the export file.
data_description.panel_export_rename_rases: Apply RAS names from the export file.

polling.name: Object polling
polling.description: The integration is event-driven and does a full sync at startup. Polling is only needed where the panel does not send events.

data_description.poll_interval: How often the enabled groups below are polled. Lower values react faster but put more load on the panel; higher values may miss short-lived changes between polls.
data_description.runtime_poll_inputs: Useful for motion detectors: PIRs generally do not send seal events, so polling is the only way to see them. A short interval is normal here.
data_description.runtime_poll_areas: Not normally needed. Areas report arm, disarm and alarm changes as events.
data_description.runtime_poll_relays: Not normally needed. Relays report changes as events, provided output events are enabled on the panel's comms path.
data_description.runtime_poll_doors: Not normally needed. Doors report lock, secure and contact changes as events, and a full door sweep runs at startup.

door_polling.name: Door polling detail
door_polling.description: Only used when runtime door polling is enabled above.

data_description.door_status_mode: Round-robin polls a few doors each cycle, which avoids asking a large system for every door at once. Only used when door polling is enabled.
data_description.door_status_per_cycle: How many doors to poll each cycle in round-robin mode. Only used when door polling is enabled.

user_sync.name: User name sync
user_sync.description: Fetch user names from the panel so access events show who badged instead of a user number.

data_description.user_sync_enabled: Reads the panel's user list so access events show a name instead of a number. Only user numbers and names are read; card and PIN data in the panel's records is never extracted.
data_description.user_sync_on_startup: Refresh the user list each time the integration starts. Names are cached, so this is only needed to pick up newly added users.
data_description.user_sync_periodic_enabled: Also refresh on a schedule. Useful where users are added regularly.
data_description.user_sync_interval_hours: How often to refresh when periodic re-sync is enabled.
data_description.user_name_order: Panels are often loaded with names surname first so the panel's own list sorts usefully. Swapping presents them given name first in Home Assistant. Only names of exactly two words are swapped, so descriptive entries such as "Card 3 Lock Box" are left alone.

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.description: Timing, session and compatibility settings. The defaults suit almost every installation — change these only if you have a specific reason.

data_description.send_acks: Acknowledges panel events so they are cleared from its queue. Disabling this will cause the panel's event queue to back up.
data_description.send_heartbeats: Keeps the comms path alive while idle, matching CTPlus behaviour.
data_description.heartbeat_interval: How often to send a keepalive. Also sets the receive watchdog, which restarts the transport after four missed intervals.
data_description.min_send_interval_ms: Paces outgoing frames so the panel's queue can keep up. Lower values are faster but give the panel less breathing room.
data_description.panel_ack_delay_ms: Waits briefly before acknowledging a panel event, matching the timing observed from CTPlus. Raise it slightly if an older panel behaves poorly with instant acknowledgements.
data_description.periodic_session_refresh_enabled: Re-establishes the command path on a schedule. Worth enabling if commands such as opening a door stop working after a long uptime while events keep arriving.
data_description.periodic_session_refresh_hours: How often to re-establish the session when periodic refresh is enabled.
data_description.quiet_mode_enabled: Suppresses recalls while the panel is repeatedly retrying an event. Left off by most installations.
data_description.input_mapping_mode: Warning: only change this if you know you need to. CTPlus is the confirmed correct mapping. The other modes exist only for setups that depended on older 2.x behaviour and will report inputs incorrectly otherwise.

error.host_required: Enter the panel host or IP address in Connection.

error.encryption_key_required: Enter the encryption key, or select None if the panel path is not encrypted.

data_description.min_send_interval_ms: Paces outgoing frames so the panel's queue can keep up. Lower values are faster but give the panel less breathing room.
data_description.panel_ack_delay_ms: Waits briefly before acknowledging a panel event, matching the timing observed from CTPlus. Raise it slightly if an older panel behaves poorly with instant acknowledgements.
data_description.periodic_session_refresh_enabled: Re-establishes the command path on a schedule. Worth enabling if commands such as opening a door stop working after a long uptime while events keep arriving.
data_description.periodic_session_refresh_hours: How often to re-establish the session when periodic refresh is enabled.
data_description.quiet_mode_enabled: Suppresses recalls while the panel is repeatedly retrying an event. Left off by most installations.
data_description.input_mapping_mode: Warning: only change this if you know you need to. CTPlus is the confirmed correct mapping. The other modes exist only for setups that depended on older 2.x behaviour and will report inputs incorrectly otherwise.
data_description.user_name_order: Panels are often loaded with names surname first so the panel's own list sorts usefully. Swapping presents them given name first in Home Assistant. Only names of exactly two words are swapped, so descriptive entries such as "Card 3 Lock Box" are left alone.

error.too_long: Too long for the panel's field.
error.security_password_format: The security / computer password must be exactly 10 digits (0-9). If the panel still uses its default, enter 0000000000.
error.key_too_long: The encryption key is longer than this encryption type allows.
error.key_not_alphanumeric: The encryption key must contain ASCII letters (A-Z, a-z) and digits (0-9) only, with no spaces or symbols.
error.host_required: Enter the panel host or IP address in Connection.
error.auth_username_required: Enter the path user name in Authentication and encryption.
error.auth_username_ascii: The path user name must contain ASCII characters only.
error.auth_username_too_long: The path user name must be no more than 30 characters.
error.auth_password_ascii: The path password must contain ASCII characters only.
error.auth_password_too_long: The path password must be no more than 16 characters.
error.encryption_key_required: Enter the encryption key, or select None if the panel path is not encrypted.

download_users.name: Sync users from panel
download_users.description: Fetch the panel's user list so access events can show user names instead of numbers. Only user numbers and names are read; card and PIN data is not.

force_arm_area.name: Force arm area
force_arm_area.description: Arm an area regardless of unsealed inputs. The normal arm action validates first and is refused by the panel if anything is unsealed.
